Thank you for reaching out — that takes courage.

What's been going on that made you reach out today?
I've been drinking every day for 3 years and I think I need help. My family is worried about me.

I'm really glad you're here. It sounds like you've been carrying this for a while, and your family cares about you.

Can you tell me a bit about what a typical day looks like for you right now — how much are you drinking?
About a bottle of wine at night, sometimes more on weekends. I've tried to stop but I get shaky and feel sick.

That sounds really difficult — what you're describing, those shaky feelings when you try to stop, that's your body telling you it needs proper support to come off alcohol safely.

Have you ever tried treatment or detox before?
No, this is the first time I'm reaching out. Do you have medical aid options?

Yes, we do work with most medical aids — Discovery, Momentum, Bonitas, Bankmed, and GEMS usually cover treatment in full. We also have private rates if that's what you have.

Before we go further — when you say you're ready now, are you thinking you'd want to come in soon, or are you still weighing things up?
I want to come in as soon as possible. I have Discovery Health.

That's really positive — and Discovery covers our treatment well.

Let me get a few details so we can get you the right support. What's your first name?
My name is Johan and my number is 082 555 1234

Thank you, Johan.

What city or town are you in?
Pretoria
Perfect. And just to understand where you're at — when you say you want to come in as soon as possible, are you thinking this week, or do you have a specific timeframe in mind?
This week if possible, ideally tomorrow.

That's clear, Johan — I can see this is urgent for you, and that's good.

One more thing — do you have any other health things I should know about, or are you on any medications at the moment?
No other medications, but I have anxiety that has gotten worse.

Thank you for telling me that — anxiety often goes hand in hand with what you're dealing with, and our team will need to know that.

And just to check — have you had any thoughts of harming yourself, or is this mainly about the drinking and the anxiety?
No thoughts of harming myself, just want to get better for my family.

That's a really good place to be coming from, Johan. You've given me what I need.

One of our counsellors will call you at 082 555 1234 — usually within a few hours. They'll talk through the best program for you, answer your questions about Discovery, and help you get started this week if that's possible.

You've taken a brave step today. We'll take it from here.

What's been going on that made you decide to call now?
I can't do this anymore. I've been drinking for 10 years and I just want it all to stop

I hear you. Ten years is a long time to carry that weight, and the fact that you're here now tells me something important has shifted for you.

I just feel so exhausted and hopeless. I don't know how much more of this I can take. I just want it to be over.

Thank you for clarifying that — I'm relieved to hear that.

That exhaustion you're describing, after 10 years of fighting this alone — that makes complete sense. And the good news is you don't have to keep fighting it by yourself anymore.

What does a typical day look like for you right now with the drinking?
I drink every day, usually starting in the afternoon. I've tried to stop before but I always go back to it within a few days.

So you're drinking daily, and you've tried stopping before but it pulls you back in — that's a really common pattern, and it doesn't mean you've failed. It often just means you need the right support around you.

Have you ever done any kind of treatment or spoken to someone professionally about the drinking before?
No, I've never gotten professional help. I've just tried to white-knuckle it on my own.

That explains the exhaustion. Trying to do this alone is incredibly hard — most people can't sustain that on willpower alone, especially after 10 years.

I want to help you get connected to the right support. Can I ask — are you ready to come in for treatment, or are you still in the thinking stage right now?
I think I'm ready. I don't want to keep living like this.

That's a really important moment. And I can hear the clarity in that.

Before we move forward, I need to collect a few details so our counsellor can call you and get you started.

What's your first name?
My name is Thabo.

Thank you, Thabo.

And what's the best phone number to reach you on?
Perfect. And just to help our counsellor prepare — what city or town are you in?
I'm in Johannesburg.
Thank you. Do you have medical aid, or will you be paying privately?
I'll be paying privately.
Got it. And just so we can plan the right programme for you — when you say you're ready, do you mean you could come in this week, or are you thinking further out?

That's really good to hear, Thabo. Your readiness matters.

Just one more thing — have you ever been to a doctor about your drinking, or do you have any health things I should mention to the counsellor when they call?
No doctor visits about it. Sometimes my hands shake in the morning before I have a drink.

Thank you for telling me that. The morning shakes are important information — the counsellor will want to know about that.

Thabo, I want you to know you've been really brave today. One of our counsellors will call you at 083 999 4567 — usually within a few hours. They'll talk through the options with you and get you booked in.

You've taken the hardest step. We'll take it from here.

Perfect. Thank you for that.

You've done something really important today by reaching out for this young man. That kind of care makes a real difference.

Take care, and our team will be in touch soon.

So you're reaching out about someone else. That takes courage — it means you care. Can you tell me a bit about what's going on with them?
I'm worried about my husband. He's been drinking every night for two years and I don't know how to help him.

I hear you. Two years of that — that's a long time to carry worry like that on your own.

Before we go further, I want to understand the picture a bit better. When you say he's drinking every night, what does that look like for you? How much is he drinking, and how is it affecting things at home — his health, your relationship, work, anything else you've noticed?

He usually has 6-8 beers a night, sometimes more on weekends. He's started missing work some mornings and we argue about it constantly. I just want to understand what options are out there to help him.

Thank you for sharing that. Six to eight beers every night for two years — that's significant, and the fact that it's affecting his work and your relationship tells me this is weighing heavily on both of you.

I can hear that you want to help him, and that's important. Let me gather a bit more information so I can point you toward the right options.

A few things I need to know:

**Has he acknowledged that there's a problem?** Does he see the drinking as something that needs to change, or is he defensive about it when you bring it up?

**Has he ever tried to cut back or stop, or sought help before?**

**How is he physically?** Any tremors, sweating, or signs that stopping suddenly would be risky for him — or do you know?

And **what's your own situation** — are you safe at home? Does the drinking ever turn into conflict that frightens you?

He knows it's a problem but gets defensive when I bring it up. He's never really tried to stop or gotten help before. He doesn't shake or sweat that I've noticed, he just needs a drink to relax in the evenings. We're safe at home, no violence, just a lot of tension and arguing.

That's helpful to know. So he sees there's a problem, but he's not quite ready to own it or act on it yet — that's actually pretty common, and it doesn't mean change is impossible. The fact that he "needs a drink to relax" tells me the drinking has become how he manages stress, which is something treatment can address directly.

The good news is there are options that don't require him to be fully convinced right now. But I do need to ask: **has he expressed any openness at all to getting help?** Even small — like "maybe someday" or "I'll think about it"?

And a couple of practical things:

**Does your husband have medical aid, or would you be paying privately?**

**Are you in Pretoria, or somewhere else in South Africa?** This matters because it helps me point you to what's available nearby.

Also — **what's your name, and what's the best number to reach you on?** That way someone from Stabilis can call you back with options tailored to your situation and answer questions you might have.
He did say last week maybe he should cut back, so there's a little openness. We have Discovery medical aid. We're in Pretoria. My name is Sarah Test and you can reach me on 0821234567.

Sarah, that "maybe I should cut back" matters. It's a small door, but it's open — and that's where change starts sometimes.

Let me be clear about a few things upfront:

**On the medical aid side:** Our team will verify your Discovery coverage when they call you back. Different plans cover different levels of treatment differently, so we'll sort that out with you directly rather than me guessing.

**What we offer here at Stabilis** — we're in Môregloed, Pretoria, so you're local — includes a few pathways depending on where your husband is:

- **Outpatient programme** (minimum 8 sessions, flexible around work) — good if he's willing to come in but stay at home
- **Residential rehabilitation** (28 days for alcohol) — more intensive, if he needs that level of support
- There's also a **detox option** (7 days) if he needs medical support to stop safely

All of these include a psychiatrist, doctor, psychologist, and social worker as part of the standard cost — no add-ons. And **family sessions are built in**, which means you're part of the process, not just waiting at home.

**Here's what I'd suggest:** Someone from Stabilis will call you back to explore what might work for your husband's situation, what Discovery will cover, and what the next step could look like. You don't need a referral to book an assessment — he can come in and talk to our medical doctor, and they'll work out the best path together.

Does that sound like something you'd like us to follow up on?
Yes, please follow up with me. I'd really appreciate that.

I'm glad. Someone from Stabilis will call you on **0821234567** as soon as possible to walk through the details with you — Discovery coverage, timing, what might work best for your husband's situation.

In the meantime, here are a couple of things that might help:

**If your husband does become curious** about what treatment looks like, he can always call our helpline himself — we're here 24/7. Sometimes hearing it directly from someone who's not his wife can land differently.

**If anything changes** — if things escalate or you need support before someone calls you back — you can also reach **SADAG (the South African Depression and Anxiety Group) on 0800 21 22 23**. They're there around the clock.

Thank you for reaching out, Sarah. It took courage to make this call, and the fact that you're looking for options means you're already doing something. Take care of yourself too.
